problem: Imitation-learned visual navigation policies (GNM/ViNT/NoMaD style) map RGB directly to robot-centric trajectories. When trained on cross-platform data, the image-to-trajectory correspondence depends on each platform's camera geometry (intrinsics, pitch, height), so the policy must infer that geometry implicitly, which is an ill-posed problem. Imitation also leaves intermediate planning decisions implicit: where to advance locally, and how to get there safely. Viewpoint augmentation or randomization (ExAug, RoVi-Aug, RING) only widens the training distribution. Depth-based planning cues (ViPlanner, NavDP) are unavailable to RGB-only deployment.
motivation: Heterogeneous multi-robot navigation datasets are the main source of scale, but the same trajectory label lands on different image regions on different platforms. This inconsistency hinders learning and generalization to unseen camera setups. The paper argues that a canonical, camera-consistent representation space is needed. Inside that space, planning supervision (safety and local progress) can then be applied consistently across all demonstrations, even though inference uses only RGB.
key_idea: Warp every image into a canonical front-facing pinhole view and express goals and trajectories in camera-height-normalized coordinates, so that image-trajectory correspondence is platform-invariant. Then add training-only safety and 'Scope-of-Reach' local-progress losses, derived from offline traversability pseudo-labels, to a diffusion trajectory policy.
insight: Projection of a ground point in a pitch-free canonical camera depends only on y/x and h/x. Rotating the image by pitch, re-projecting with fixed intrinsics and dividing trajectories by camera height therefore removes the camera-geometry nuisance variable exactly, for flat ground and a front-centered camera. The ablation (Table 2) shows canonicalization alone gives a modest gain for plain imitation: 62.6→65.6 SR at CitySim 20m and 67.0→70.0 at AWS 12m. Its larger role is as an enabler. Applying safety and progress supervision without canonicalization (S+P) reaches only 77.1/75.2 SR with std across camera configs of 7.7/7.6, versus 86.4/85.5 with std 3.8/3.9 for C+S+P. Safety supervision is the largest single gain in outdoor CitySim (65.6→83.0), and SoR progress supervision in the indoor hospital (70.0→81.2). Pretrained DINOv3+LoRA over training from scratch is also critical (28.8→62.6 at CitySim 20m). Under pitch change, CanonNav's SR varies by only 1.17 pp at CitySim 20m, versus drops of 24.66 pp (LiMo) and 50.34 pp (ViPlanner).
method: Camera geometry canonicalization: assuming a front-centered camera, geometry is φ=(K, R_pitch, h). Images are warped by the homography K̃ R_pitch^{-1} K^{-1} to a canonical 336×256 view (f̃x=f̃y=c̃x=168, c̃y=128). Trajectories and goals are divided by camera height, (x/h, y/h) and (r/h, θ). Random yaw (±15°) and flip augmentation are applied consistently to images and trajectories.

Policy network: DINOv3 ViT-S+ with LoRA (rank 3); features from layers {3,6,9,12} are aggregated into a 256×16×21 map. A goal MLP produces a query for multi-head cross-attention over the image features. The conditioning vector f_cond=[pooled image, goal, attended] (768-d) drives a conditional 1D U-Net diffusion policy (DDPM, 10 denoising steps) that outputs B=30 candidates of N=16 height-normalized waypoints.

Offline pseudo-labels (training only): a frozen ViTA traversability estimator produces per-pixel masks. These are projected with the known camera geometry onto a flat-ground BEV collision map (±32 m lateral, 32 m forward, 0.1 m cells) and then turned into a metric SDF. The SoR target is the last sampled expert pose before the robot footprint is ≥30% occupied or the pose leaves the FoV.

Safety supervision: a collision loss on the one-step denoised estimate τ̂0 applies a softplus penalty on (d_safe − SDF) at each metric waypoint, aggregated by log-sum-exp (d_safe=0.75). A lightweight traversability head takes stop-gradient, bilinearly sampled image features plus waypoint coordinates and is trained with BCE. Targets are 1 if SDF > robot radius 0.25, else 0; out-of-view waypoints get 0.5.

Local-progress (Scope-of-Reach) supervision: a head predicts a BEV Gaussian (μ̃, σ̃), height-normalized, of where to advance. L_pred is Gaussian NLL + SmoothL1 to the SoR target. L_neg penalizes SoR probability mass on collision cells. L_cons is a soft-min Mahalanobis distance that pulls at least one generated waypoint toward the SoR. The total loss is 25·L_diff + safety + progress + 0.05·smoothness.

Inference path selection: per-segment traversability scores are treated as unit-length survival probabilities, giving an expected reachable length and an expected reach point p̄. Each candidate is scored 0.6·goal-advance + 0.4·displacement + 0.2·temporal-consistency, and the best is executed. The EMA model runs onboard at 4.5 Hz on a Jetson AGX Orin.

setting.backbone: DINOv3 ViT-S+ image encoder (LoRA-adapted) + conditional 1D U-Net diffusion policy + SoR/traversability MLP heads (trained)
setting.model_size: DINOv3 ViT-S+ encoder (LoRA rank 3) + 1D U-Net; total parameter count not reported
setting.training_data: 8.35M image-goal-trajectory pairs from SCAND, HuRoN, BotanicGarden, the authors' own real-world Husky data and simulated HM3D data. Safety and SoR pseudo-labels come from the offline ViTA traversability estimator (training only). Trained 70 epochs, batch size 256, AdamW, EMA.
setting.observation: monocular RGB (single frame) + relative point goal (r, θ); known camera intrinsics, pitch and height used for canonicalization
setting.action_space: predicted robot-centric 2D trajectory: 16 waypoints, height-normalized; 30 sampled candidates, one selected
setting.simulator: Gazebo (CitySim outdoor, AWS RoboMaker Hospital indoor) for evaluation; HM3D sim data used in training
setting.privileged: none at inference (RGB only, no depth or maps). Requires camera calibration (K, pitch, height) for canonicalization and a relative point goal. Depth and traversability pseudo-labels are used only during training.

numbers_note: There are no standard embodied-navigation benchmarks. Evaluation uses the authors' own Gazebo CitySim (with added clutter) and AWS Hospital point-goal protocols plus real-world trials. Ablation results (Table 2) are reported only for the longest subgoal interval (CitySim 20m, AWS 12m). Per-camera-config ΔSR results for hFoV and pitch are given only in a figure (Fig. 3). The text quotes that CanonNav varies by 1.17 pp under pitch change at CitySim 20m (max 3.87 pp at AWS 9m), versus LiMo −24.66 pp, ViPlanner −50.34 pp and NavDP +9.80 pp.
results: With RGB only, CanonNav reaches the highest SR at the longest subgoal intervals: 86.4% at CitySim 20m and 85.5% at AWS Hospital 12m. The strongest baseline is the RGB-D NavDP at 71.2% and 82.9%; CanonNav also cuts CitySim-20m collisions from 2.21 to 0.89 per 100 m. It far exceeds the best RGB baseline LiMo (48.3% / 39.7%) and stays close to NavDP at short intervals (99.4 vs 99.7, 97.1 vs 98.3). On a real Husky it succeeds in 41/50 trials with 0.26 interventions per subgoal, versus 17/50 and 1.58 for NavDP.
limitations: If the original camera's FoV is wider than the predefined canonical view, canonicalization discards visual context. The method also assumes a front-centered camera (pitch + height only), flat ground for pseudo-labels, and requires known calibration.
It handles camera geometry but not embodiment-specific policy differences. Robot radius and safety margin are fixed at training, so a new platform requires retraining.

Failures mostly come from wrong Scope-of-Reach predictions for obstacles that are rare in training or visually ambiguous. Evaluation is point-goal only, in custom Gazebo scenes and small real-world trials, not on standard benchmarks.
